title: Dynamic resolution without oscillation (hysteresis and cooldown)
player_outcome: No repeated hitches from the 3D resolution flipping up and down on mid-range GPUs. The picture stays stable and steps down only when it really must.
design: Checked in code: DynamicResolution looks at 30-frame windows and steps down when a frame is slow and GPU-bound, but steps up as soon as GPU time is under 11 ms, with no cooldown and no prediction (DynamicResolution.cs:56-64). Each Scaling3DScale change reallocates viewport buffers, so it oscillates and hitches.

Add src/Strata.Core/Presentation/ResolutionGovernor.cs (pure and testable), fed (frameMs, gpuMs) every frame. It uses 30-frame windows and excludes frames over 50 ms (CPU hitches such as saves). It steps down one level after 2 consecutive slow, GPU-bound windows. It steps up only when predicted GPU time at the next level (gpu × (next/current)²) stays under 12 ms for 4 windows and at least 8 s have passed since the last down-step. Levels are quantized to {1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6}, capped at the preset RenderScale, with at least 3 s between any two changes.
DynamicResolution.cs uses the governor, applies FSR once when leaving 1.0, times changes as gd.dynres.change, and exposes a render.scale_changes probe.
files_add: tests/Strata.Core.Tests/Presentation/ResolutionGovernorTests.cs — oscillation, overload, recovery and hitch cases
tests: ResolutionGovernorTests.NoOscillationNearThresholds: GPU alternating 11-14 ms gives at most 1 change per 10 s
ResolutionGovernorTests.HitchFramesIgnored: a 200 ms frame does not trigger a step
verification: Rendering run on a mid GPU with --graphics=ultra: F3 '3D scale' stays stable while standing still; render.scale_changes stays small over 5 minutes
risks: Headless has no GPU timing: the governor is a no-op there, as today
Slower reaction to real overload (by design); tune the window counts
